# Predicting the next scene is not the same as acting or preserving a world

[简体中文](../../../../learning/deep-dives/multimodal-models/world-state-actions.md) · English

Updated 2026-11-26 · 39 topic entries / 23 representative comparisons

World models must separately show what state retains, how actions alter futures, how plans are evaluated, and how memory persists across segments. LeWAM and V-JEPA Policy connect prediction and actions; prediction–planning evaluation decomposes errors; WOVEN supervises visual transitions; PPMem maintains geometry; VBVR-Pro executes task checks. SWIM learns relative state-coordinate weights from offline action predictability to shape latent distances without giving deployment planners real future states.

[Mechanisms](#comparison) · [Trade-offs](#analysis) · [Cross-paper questions](#questions) · [Updates](#updates)

!!! note "How to read this card"

    The table compares representative methods. It is not a shared-benchmark leaderboard. Teaching examples are not measured results.

Axes: Future latents, actions, visual transitions, or persistent geometry · Jointly shaped or frozen vision encoders · Latent loss, physical state error, or actual planning success · Candidate generation, executable constraints, and cross-view consistency

## Trade-off analysis {#analysis}

### Readable state, predictable futures, and successful action are separate checks

LeWAM jointly shapes vision with control and prediction; V-JEPA Policy learns prediction/actions on frozen vision. Either way, test if latents retain physical state, how much additional error prediction adds, and whether planning succeeds. A common physical decoder separates the first two; planning is run independently rather than inferred from latent loss.

Sources: [LeWAM: End-to-End World and Action Modeling with JEPAs](../../../../reproductions/2610.12818-lewam/README-en.md) · [V-JEPA Policy: Building Effective World-Action Models on Predictive Visual Latents](../../../../foundation-models/2609.37250-vjepa-policy/README-en.md) · [One-Step Prediction Fidelity Is a Poor Proxy for Planning Performance in JEPA World Models](../../../../foundation-models/2610.19375-jepa-prediction-planning/README-en.md)

### Generating plausible transitions and verifying consistency need separate interfaces

WOVEN supplies generated video transitions whose visible changes must actually supervise learning instead of revealing outcomes in prompts. PPMem preserves geometry across chunks and views; future camera paths do not reveal real future frames. VBVR-Pro checks executable constraints, but a scorer does not train a capable generator. These are data, memory, and verification respectively.

Sources: [WOVEN: Weaving Visual World Modeling into Multimodal LLMs](../../../../reproductions/2610.12417-woven/README-en.md) · [Persistent Planar Memory for Video World Models](../../../../foundation-models/2610.23795-ppmem/README-en.md) · [VBVR-Pro: A Scalable and Verifiable Suite for Native Visual Reasoning](../../../../reproductions/2608.26105-vbvr-pro/README-en.md)

### October 29: new method and evidence boundary

GUI-JEPA predicts residual successors in current screen latents and combines action-specific ROI/global regions and structural cosine scores. This differs from pixel-video supervision and actual GUI execution. The component receives external frozen latents and text matching scores, retains a trained three-layer predictor and head, and does not use positive training labels to choose actions in forward inference.

Sources: [LeWAM: End-to-End World and Action Modeling with JEPAs](../../../../reproductions/2610.12818-lewam/README-en.md) · [GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latents as a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents](../../../../foundation-models/2610.36877-gui-jepa/README-en.md)

### Behavior can shape geometry without becoming a future-state oracle

GUI-JEPA predicts candidate-conditioned latent residuals and learns listwise decision scoring. SWIM uses offline action chunks to learn which state displacements predict those actions, then freezes continuous gates as supervision for latent geometry. Neither latent check establishes execution. SWIM's h changes future-state spacing, not the fixed current action chunk. Inverse dynamics and true future states stay out of planning; coordinate standardization after `sqrt(g)` cancels the weights.

Sources: [SWIM: Learning What Matters from Behaviors for JEPA World Models](../../../../foundation-models/2610.36662-swim/README-en.md) · [GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latents as a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents](../../../../foundation-models/2610.36877-gui-jepa/README-en.md)

### JEPA representation alignment and a world-action loop require different supervision

RS-JEPA aligns registered sensor images and scan views for retrieval. Its adversarial partitions and neighborhood loss describe relationships among current scenes, not action-conditioned state transitions merely because its name includes JEPA. V-JEPA Policy freezes a pretrained encoder and trains a future-latent predictor and action expert, requiring separate action/environment validation. Remote-sensing F1@5, latent prediction error and robot success cannot be combined into one score.

Sources: [RS-JEPA: Remote Sensing Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture with Scan-Path Views for Cross-Sensor Image Retrieval](../../../../multimodal-models/2611.14496-rs-jepa/README-en.md) · [V-JEPA Policy: Building Effective World-Action Models on Predictive Visual Latents](../../../../foundation-models/2609.37250-vjepa-policy/README-en.md)

### The invariant content across views can be scene or action

RS-JEPA matches the same scene across sensors and aligns neighbourhoods. OnlyAct pulls together scene-changed action-preserving pairs while contrasting different times in the same scene. Their needs for scene identity differ; one generic InfoNCE cannot establish both. OnlyAct's pairing depends on flow and camera-motion assumptions. Passing CUDA candidate-mask and gradient checks does not validate these semantic assumptions.

Sources: [OnlyAct: Extracting Action Representations from Foundation Models for World Models](../../../../multimodal-models/2611.14420-onlyact/README-en.md) · [RS-JEPA: Remote Sensing Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture with Scan-Path Views for Cross-Sensor Image Retrieval](../../../../multimodal-models/2611.14496-rs-jepa/README-en.md)

### Action-conditioned forecasts do not identify interventions or complete control

LeWAM jointly learns representations and action flow matching, then rolls out frozen dynamics, refines actions by gradients, and receives environment feedback. Its current local evidence remains non-holdout diagnostics with no measured planning advantage. SensorWM learns conditional trajectories from observational wearables and normalizes projected gain by individual behavioral variability. It explicitly does not identify causal intervention effects, and offline coach preferences are not health outcomes. Prediction, selection, execution, and effects require different evidence; the local ranking kernel cannot replace the missing model.

Sources: [Personalized health coaching via coachable health age and counterfactual wearable trajectories](../../../../multimodal-models/2611.08568-sensorwm-planning/README-en.md) · [LeWAM: End-to-End World and Action Modeling with JEPAs](../../../../reproductions/2610.12818-lewam/README-en.md)

### Generating video and learning transitions require separate acceptance

A video generator can supply transition-training data, but visual quality, action fidelity, state consistency and downstream reasoning need separate checks. The full 14B/1.3-million-clip PixVid matrix is not run. Existing small WOVEN SFT negative results do not predict PixVid benefits. No local joint system is claimed.

Sources: [Back to Pixels: Lifting Latent Video Diffusion into Pixel Space](../../../../multimodal-models/2611.17336-pixvid/README-en.md) · [WOVEN: Weaving Visual World Modeling into Multimodal LLMs](../../../../reproductions/2610.12417-woven/README-en.md)

### Transition supervision is not a continual evaluation of what should change

WOVEN controls scene/action/reasoning for training and generalization, putting real visual transitions into response-only SFT; the repository retains a negative small grouped result. Stratified Retention distinguishes expired facts from structural forgetting: invariants may be corrected but should not degrade, while instance positions must update promptly. Combining the ideas would require predeclared strata, per-round probes and new-episode revision traces. No such model experiment is run here; the component only rejects leakage and censoring confounds.

Sources: [What Should World Models Forget? Stratified Retention for Continual Adaptation](../../../../foundation-models/2610.03713-stratified-retention-protocol/README-en.md) · [WOVEN: Weaving Visual World Modeling into Multimodal LLMs](../../../../reproductions/2610.12417-woven/README-en.md)

### Fresh capture and unseen scenes are not the same generalization control

WOVEN groups initial-frame sources to keep related actions/questions out of different splits. RSLiveBench-UAV requires captures between consecutive releases and retires the earliest admitted scene. Renewal reduces exposure to old answers without removing scene bias; generated-scene OOD does not provide real aerial geometry. Tiny FIFO replay only validates timing and denominators, not spatial VLM capability or full benchmark integration.

Sources: [RSLiveBench-UAV: A Continually Evolving Vision-Language Benchmark for Aerial Spatial Intelligence](../../../../multimodal-models/2611.14953-rslivebench-uav-protocol/README-en.md) · [WOVEN: Weaving Visual World Modeling into Multimodal LLMs](../../../../reproductions/2610.12417-woven/README-en.md)

### Learning controllable dynamics and preserving numerical rollouts are different axes

The reviewed LeWAM README specifies joint action-flow, latent-MSE and SIGReg training; planning updates actions only and selects by unpenalized goal cost. Its training-trajectory goals remain non-holdout diagnostics. WM-Quant instead freezes the backbone and calibrates encoder/step-specific predictor ranges, retains floating controls and uses the integer-zero-point lattice in Equations1–2. Shared action-conditioned rollouts do not make dynamics training, planning and PTQ calibration interchangeable evidence. The tiny local calibrator does not quantize LeWAM or compare robot success.

Sources: [WM-Quant: Rollout-Aware Post-Training Quantization for JEPA-Style World Models](../../../../foundation-models/2611.21882-wm-quant/README-en.md) · [LeWAM: End-to-End World and Action Modeling with JEPAs](../../../../reproductions/2610.12818-lewam/README-en.md)

### DWD: separate final pixel readout from denoising

PixVid transfers a latent DiT to pixel-space inputs/generation with a detailer. DWD retains latent sampling and changes final readout. Pixel output does not mean pixel-space sampling. Pixel and trajectory terms sample different timestep distributions, accumulating gradients before one optimizer step. Final pixel readout omits CFG because it no longer advances the trajectory. Treating t0as a conventional decoder degrades quality in the paper.

Sources: [Decoding Without a Decoder: Direct Pixel Prediction from Diffusion Transformers](../../../../multimodal-models/2611.22287-dwd/README-en.md) · [Back to Pixels: Lifting Latent Video Diffusion into Pixel Space](../../../../multimodal-models/2611.17336-pixvid/README-en.md)

### Counterfactual World Models: JEPAs That Reason About "What If"

DT-JEPA predicts future latent distributions from history for decision making; true futures appear only in training. CWM answers alternative actions after a factual outcome is observed. It cannot access an unobserved future, and a DT-JEPA mean is not automatically an individual counterfactual. The observed input follows the factual action; the true alternative outcome is never an algorithm input. Transport-then-decode differs from decoding each term before transport. Coordinate guarantees need readout assumptions. Error is individual-minus-average action effect, not simply factual-model prediction error.

Sources: [Counterfactual World Models: JEPAs That Reason About "What If"](../../../../foundation-models/2611.24778-counterfactual-wm/README-en.md) · [DT-JEPA: Learning to Predict Future Representations for Decision-Making](../../../../foundation-models/2610.32657-dt-jepa/README-en.md)

### Autoregressive View Model

CWM changes an action after an observed event and reuses its disturbance residual. AVM continues camera-conditioned generation with retrieved history. Scene-revisit consistency does not establish identifiable same-disturbance counterfactuals. The notation summarizes the paper flow objective and context retrieval, not a new algorithm. Retrieved history includes both observations and model-generated views. No explicit3D representation does not mean no geometric conditioning: cameras, time and context roles still matter.

Sources: [Autoregressive View Model](../../../../multimodal-models/2611.23417-autoregressive-view-model/README-en.md) · [Counterfactual World Models: JEPAs That Reason About "What If"](../../../../foundation-models/2611.24778-counterfactual-wm/README-en.md)

### JEPA Dots: Dual-Latent World Model for Language-Guided Robot Control

LeWAM jointly models worlds/actions and plans through prediction. JEPA Dots separates language goals from fixed-action dynamics and does not use its world branch for deployment action search. Shared masked-MoT ancestry does not imply identical inference. The invariance is a forward-conditioning property, not statistical independence after joint backbone training. The world branch supplies training supervision; deployment generates eight actions by action flow and executes the first two before replanning, rather than searching actions through the world model.

Sources: [JEPA Dots: Dual-Latent World Model for Language-Guided Robot Control](../../../../multimodal-models/2611.24062-jepa-dots/README-en.md) · [LeWAM: End-to-End World and Action Modeling with JEPAs](../../../../reproductions/2610.12818-lewam/README-en.md)

### MV-JEPA: Post-Training Video Encoders for Cross-View Understanding

Time-JEPA supplies physical time-series targets through masked latent prediction and unmasked physical-state regression on one online encoder. MV-JEPA instead predicts another camera's latent targets through a joint predictor over independently encoded context views. Both keep training targets out of inference inputs, but cross-view queries are not Time-JEPA's sensor head; replay-based retention and physical-time alignment require different checks. The EMA teacher encodes full context and held-out observations; targets receive per-token LayerNorm and stop-gradient. Contexts receive distinct randomly assigned view IDs, while held-out queries have a reserved ID; the two query types use separate mask embeddings. Eq4 gives equal weight to masked-context and all held-out target tokens, normalizing each example before averaging the batch. It is neither view-wise averaging nor a batch-wide micro-average. Each epoch shuffles152multiview and148original single-view replay updates with shared online encoder/predictor. Teacher EMA follows the optimizer at momentum0.99925.

Sources: [MV-JEPA: Post-Training Video Encoders for Cross-View Understanding](../../../../foundation-models/2611.25172-mv-jepa/README-en.md) · [Time-JEPA: Grounding Video World Models with Physical Time Series](../../../../foundation-models/2610.23982-time-jepa/README-en.md)

### CriticJEPA: World Models Are Better Critics Than Optimizers

Prediction-planning evaluation separates representation readability, prediction error and execution success. CriticJEPA further distinguishes candidate sources, rankings and optimization under one frozen model. Neither substitutes latent loss for execution. CriticJEPA additionally needs trained flows and temporal hierarchy contracts; fixed candidates are diagnostic, not capability implementations. The final critic retains H-JEPA's target space, scoring windows and action-consistency term. The first predicted upper state becomes the subgoal. Paper FLOPs include backpropagation, not wall time. The18-model multi-domain matrix is terminally cost-deferred locally, with no operator, environment execution or automatic retry.

Sources: [CriticJEPA: World Models Are Better Critics Than Optimizers](../../../../foundation-models/2611.32357-criticjepa/README-en.md) · [One-Step Prediction Fidelity Is a Poor Proxy for Planning Performance in JEPA World Models](../../../../foundation-models/2610.19375-jepa-prediction-planning/README-en.md)

### Not all world models can doubt: how training objective and architecture shape epistemic uncertainty in JEPA and RSSM world models

Prediction-planning evaluation separates representation error, prediction error and execution. JEPA EU asks where uncertainty loses a perturbation. Low error, responsive uncertainty and planning success are different evidence. A posterior head observes the current frame and cannot replace a prior head in imagined rollout. A Laplace readout only sees its feature: a perturbation erased upstream cannot be recovered by changing that readout. The RSSM GRU admits a one-frame change through its gate and accumulates persistent changes; reconstruction allocates signal by pixels. The observation-dependent posterior feature is unavailable during imagination.

Sources: [Not all world models can doubt: how training objective and architecture shape epistemic uncertainty in JEPA and RSSM world models](../../../../foundation-models/2611.34830-jepa-eu/README-en.md) · [One-Step Prediction Fidelity Is a Poor Proxy for Planning Performance in JEPA World Models](../../../../foundation-models/2610.19375-jepa-prediction-planning/README-en.md)

### Hidden critical-path latency does not eliminate total GPU cost

Memory precedes the next prompt, boundaries select only completed prefills, and missing updates retain old memory. Future annotations are reward/evaluator-only. SFT/GRPO train the 8B selector; fixed recency is not a substitute. PixVid instead changes the generator representation. LongLive's roughly 1% added time uses extra agent/auxiliary GPUs; the six-H100 illustration, eight-B200 node and 35B/4B/8B services exceed one-card resources. Both entries are review-only: original figures/public mocks are not capability or reproduction evidence.

Sources: [Agentic LongLive: Asynchronous Agentic Memory for Long Video Generation](../../../../multimodal-models/2611.34907-agentic-longlive/README-en.md) · [Back to Pixels: Lifting Latent Video Diffusion into Pixel Space](../../../../multimodal-models/2611.17336-pixvid/README-en.md)

## Cross-paper questions {#questions}

Try answering before expanding the explanation. Each question relates at least two papers.

### Do LeWAM and V-JEPA Policy differ only in their visual backbone? {#cross-frozen-versus-joint-encoder}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. LeWAM jointly updates encoder, dynamics, and policy with online targets; V-JEPA Policy freezes pretrained vision and detaches future targets. Whether control gradients shape vision and whether targets move are different training contracts.

    **Illustrative example:** Grasping supervision can adjust vision in the joint path, while the frozen path mainly changes prediction and action modules.

    Sources: [LeWAM: End-to-End World and Action Modeling with JEPAs](../../../../reproductions/2610.12818-lewam/README-en.md) · [V-JEPA Policy: Building Effective World-Action Models on Predictive Visual Latents](../../../../foundation-models/2609.37250-vjepa-policy/README-en.md)

### Does lower JEPA prediction error show LeWAM candidate planning beats a reactive policy? {#cross-low-prediction-loss-not-planning}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. Prediction error mixes latent readability and added dynamics error; plans also depend on action candidates, accumulation, and goals. Decode with the same physical head to separate errors and test planning independently. Local non-holdout LeWAM did not observe an advantage.

    **Illustrative example:** Predicting a static scene accurately does not choose actions that reach a target.

    Sources: [One-Step Prediction Fidelity Is a Poor Proxy for Planning Performance in JEPA World Models](../../../../foundation-models/2610.19375-jepa-prediction-planning/README-en.md) · [LeWAM: End-to-End World and Action Modeling with JEPAs](../../../../reproductions/2610.12818-lewam/README-en.md)

### Which of WOVEN's videos, PPMem's geometry, and VBVR-Pro's scorer guarantees correctness? {#cross-rollout-memory-verifier}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** They serve different roles: action-conditioned transition data, persistent memory, and executable checks. Realistic video does not guarantee a valid transition, stored geometry can err, and scores cover only defined rules. Verify data, state maintenance, and scoring independently.

    **Illustrative example:** Memory may preserve object position at an old viewpoint, but counting and ordering require their own validation.

    Sources: [WOVEN: Weaving Visual World Modeling into Multimodal LLMs](../../../../reproductions/2610.12417-woven/README-en.md) · [Persistent Planar Memory for Video World Models](../../../../foundation-models/2610.23795-ppmem/README-en.md) · [VBVR-Pro: A Scalable and Verifiable Suite for Native Visual Reasoning](../../../../reproductions/2608.26105-vbvr-pro/README-en.md)

### Why isn't a GUI-JEPA successor prediction a successful action verified on a phone? {#cross-oct29-method-boundary}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** A learned latent can omit real state constraints. Success needs environment feedback; small latent forward passes, candidate permutation equivariance, and gradients verify only the module.

    **Illustrative example:** A predicted page vector near the target does not show that a real button was clickable or the request succeeded.

    Sources: [LeWAM: End-to-End World and Action Modeling with JEPAs](../../../../reproductions/2610.12818-lewam/README-en.md) · [GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latents as a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents](../../../../foundation-models/2610.36877-gui-jepa/README-en.md)

### Why may neither SWIM nor GUI-JEPA give a real successor state to a deployment policy? {#cross-swim-training-future-not-planning-oracle}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** `q(t+h)` is offline supervision for SWIM inverse dynamics and gating; only weighted latent geometry transfers to image-based planning. GUI-JEPA likewise predicts rather than observes candidate successors. Real successors would turn the evaluation into an oracle.

    **Illustrative example:** Offline future frames can label displacements, but action selection cannot see those answers. Varying h also does not stretch the fixed five-frame action target across the entire h interval.

    Sources: [SWIM: Learning What Matters from Behaviors for JEPA World Models](../../../../foundation-models/2610.36662-swim/README-en.md) · [GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latents as a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents](../../../../foundation-models/2610.36877-gui-jepa/README-en.md)

### Does consistent cross-sensor neighborhoods in RS-JEPA establish action planning? {#cross-retrieval-jepa-not-action-policy}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. They constrain registered-image retrieval representations and similarities to other scenes, without defining action-conditioned dynamics or a policy output. V-JEPA Policy adds a future predictor and flow-matching action expert. Passing representation kernels cannot replace environment-task validation.

    **Illustrative example:** Both sensors ranking similar farmland scenes consistently demonstrates agreement in representation. It predicts neither what a robot will see after moving nor which action it should take.

    Sources: [RS-JEPA: Remote Sensing Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture with Scan-Path Views for Cross-Sensor Image Retrieval](../../../../multimodal-models/2611.14496-rs-jepa/README-en.md) · [V-JEPA Policy: Building Effective World-Action Models on Predictive Visual Latents](../../../../foundation-models/2609.37250-vjepa-policy/README-en.md)

### Why can't same-scene cross-sensor pairs replace OnlyAct positives just because both methods learn representations? {#cross-cross-jepa-scene-versus-action-invariance}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Same-scene alignment retains scene identity, whereas OnlyAct retains action across scenes. Substitution changes invariance and can reward scene shortcuts. Similar InfoNCE equations do not imply equivalent pair semantics; action transfer needs independent evidence.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: SAR and optical images of one bridge suit RS-JEPA. OnlyAct instead needs the same door-opening action in different rooms, not arbitrary actions in one room.

    Sources: [OnlyAct: Extracting Action Representations from Foundation Models for World Models](../../../../multimodal-models/2611.14420-onlyact/README-en.md) · [RS-JEPA: Remote Sensing Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture with Scan-Path Views for Cross-Sensor Image Retrieval](../../../../multimodal-models/2611.14496-rs-jepa/README-en.md)

### Can a SensorWM ranking kernel and LeWAM planner share one planning-success ranking because both select a better candidate? {#cross-cross-worldmodel-ranking-versus-closed-loop-evidence}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. The SensorWM kernel only ranks external endpoints by gain over effort, without a model, medical judgment, or execution. LeWAM produces actions and executes an environment loop, yet its existing local results are not held-out capability evidence. Denominators, forecast provenance, causal meanings and execution evidence differ.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: choosing the largest of three supplied ratios neither reaches a robot goal nor improves someone's health twelve weeks later. Each outcome requires independent verification.

    Sources: [Personalized health coaching via coachable health age and counterfactual wearable trajectories](../../../../multimodal-models/2611.08568-sensorwm-planning/README-en.md) · [LeWAM: End-to-End World and Action Modeling with JEPAs](../../../../reproductions/2610.12818-lewam/README-en.md)

### Would replacing WOVEN's generator with PixVid establish stronger transition reasoning? {#cross-nov15-pixvid}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. First evaluate action/state fidelity, then train/evaluate downstream models under fixed data protocols. Image clarity covers only one axis; no such combination was run here.

    **Illustrative example:** A sharper but incorrect action outcome still supplies incorrect downstream transition supervision.

    Sources: [Back to Pixels: Lifting Latent Video Diffusion into Pixel Space](../../../../multimodal-models/2611.17336-pixvid/README-en.md) · [WOVEN: Weaving Visual World Modeling into Multimodal LLMs](../../../../reproductions/2610.12417-woven/README-en.md)

### Does lower old-scene accuracy after WOVEN training establish harmful forgetting? {#cross-nov18-stratified-retention-protocol}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. First ask whether the old answer remains true. Correctly revising stale instances differs from losing invariants. Existing grouped WOVEN accuracy does not supply per-round differential-retention evidence; it needs fixed panels, new-episode change probes and false-revision controls.

    **Illustrative example:** After a chair moves, rejecting its old coordinates may be correct. Assuming it ceases to exist when occluded violates an invariant. Final recovery cannot hide an intermediate negative flip.

    Sources: [What Should World Models Forget? Stratified Retention for Continual Adaptation](../../../../foundation-models/2610.03713-stratified-retention-protocol/README-en.md) · [WOVEN: Weaving Visual World Modeling into Multimodal LLMs](../../../../reproductions/2610.12417-woven/README-en.md)

### Does replacing a scene with yesterday's images of the same car park establish both freshness and scene-OOD? {#cross-nov18-rslivebench-uav-protocol}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Not necessarily. It can satisfy capture windows and FIFO without testing unseen scenes when location, entities and viewpoints remain similar. WOVEN's scene axis and UAV temporal controls require separate records.

    **Illustrative example:** A new capture of the same car park is a fresh observation. An unseen generated restaurant may be scene-OOD but supplies no real UAV cross-view vehicle geometry.

    Sources: [RSLiveBench-UAV: A Continually Evolving Vision-Language Benchmark for Aerial Spatial Intelligence](../../../../multimodal-models/2611.14953-rslivebench-uav-protocol/README-en.md) · [WOVEN: Weaving Visual World Modeling into Multimodal LLMs](../../../../reproductions/2610.12417-woven/README-en.md)

### Do shared JEPA rollouts mean LeWAM was quantized and validated here? {#cross-nov18-wm-quant}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. WM-Quant evaluates LeWM/DINO-WM; LeWAM is a different joint world-action model. Local checks cover the quantization lattice, multi-step range objective and control preservation, without LeWAM integration or robot evaluation.

    **Illustrative example:** LeWAM three-arm robot results cannot substitute for low-bit WM-Quant planning, and one calibration loss does not establish LeWAM planning capability.

    Sources: [WM-Quant: Rollout-Aware Post-Training Quantization for JEPA-Style World Models](../../../../foundation-models/2611.21882-wm-quant/README-en.md) · [LeWAM: End-to-End World and Action Modeling with JEPAs](../../../../reproductions/2610.12818-lewam/README-en.md)

### How does this differ from PixVid? {#cross-nov18-dwd}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** PixVid transfers inputs and the pixel generation path. DWD keeps latent denoising and adds a final output head.

    **Illustrative example:** Removing a VAE and adding a linear layer does not supply PixVid timestep mapping or its detailer.

    Sources: [Decoding Without a Decoder: Direct Pixel Prediction from Diffusion Transformers](../../../../multimodal-models/2611.22287-dwd/README-en.md) · [Back to Pixels: Lifting Latent Video Diffusion into Pixel Space](../../../../multimodal-models/2611.17336-pixvid/README-en.md)

### How does its information set differ from DT-JEPA? {#cross-nov19-counterfactual-wm}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** DT-JEPA predicts before acting from history. CWM needs the observed factual outcome. They answer different queries with different information.

    **Illustrative example:** Before the first action, its not-yet-observed outcome cannot be passed to CWM.

    Sources: [Counterfactual World Models: JEPAs That Reason About "What If"](../../../../foundation-models/2611.24778-counterfactual-wm/README-en.md) · [DT-JEPA: Learning to Predict Future Representations for Decision-Making](../../../../foundation-models/2610.32657-dt-jepa/README-en.md)

### Does revisit consistency imply CWM counterfactual ability? {#cross-nov19-autoregressive-view-model}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. Revisit persistence concerns camera paths and generated history. Individual counterfactuals require a same-disturbance coupling across actions.

    **Illustrative example:** A stable door frame says nothing about a boat’s alternative heading in the same wind.

    Sources: [Autoregressive View Model](../../../../multimodal-models/2611.23417-autoregressive-view-model/README-en.md) · [Counterfactual World Models: JEPAs That Reason About "What If"](../../../../foundation-models/2611.24778-counterfactual-wm/README-en.md)

### How does deployment differ from LeWAM? {#cross-nov19-jepa-dots}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** The JEPA Dots world branch is training supervision, while deployment uses a flow policy, not LeWAM-style world-model action optimization.

    **Illustrative example:** Executing two actions from an eight-step chunk is receding-horizon control, not gradient planning over a world cost.

    Sources: [JEPA Dots: Dual-Latent World Model for Language-Guided Robot Control](../../../../multimodal-models/2611.24062-jepa-dots/README-en.md) · [LeWAM: End-to-End World and Action Modeling with JEPAs](../../../../reproductions/2610.12818-lewam/README-en.md)

### Can MV-JEPA and Time-JEPA swap their additional targets? {#cross-nov21-mv-jepa}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. MV-JEPA predicts cross-camera latents through a joint-view predictor; Time-JEPA aligns physical sequences through an unmasked regression branch. Neither target should become a student input.

    **Illustrative example:** Illustration: a velocity scalar belongs to a physical head; back-view tokens belong to held-out queries. Replacing labels does not preserve the task.

    Sources: [MV-JEPA: Post-Training Video Encoders for Cross-View Understanding](../../../../foundation-models/2611.25172-mv-jepa/README-en.md) · [Time-JEPA: Grounding Video World Models with Physical Time Series](../../../../foundation-models/2610.23982-time-jepa/README-en.md)

### What distinction does CriticJEPA add to prediction-planning evaluation? {#cross-nov25-criticjepa}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** It changes candidate sources and search under a frozen model to separate ranking, useful gradients and execution. The evaluation protocol instead decomposes representation/prediction errors with a frozen decoder and separately requires real planning outcomes.

    **Illustrative example:** Illustration: an unchanged one-step-error model may rank flow proposals usefully but not out-of-distribution prolonged-search outputs; one-step loss alone cannot select the planner.

    Sources: [CriticJEPA: World Models Are Better Critics Than Optimizers](../../../../foundation-models/2611.32357-criticjepa/README-en.md) · [One-Step Prediction Fidelity Is a Poor Proxy for Planning Performance in JEPA World Models](../../../../foundation-models/2610.19375-jepa-prediction-planning/README-en.md)

### Does adding uncertainty remove the need for real planning evaluation? {#cross-nov26-jepa-eu}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. Error,uncertainty and success differ. JEPA EU also evaluates CEM; a posterior readout can detect observed anomalies but requires observations absent in imagined futures.

    **Illustrative example:** Illustration:detecting an anomaly with the actual next-frame posterior does not make that signal available before the action.

    Sources: [Not all world models can doubt: how training objective and architecture shape epistemic uncertainty in JEPA and RSSM world models](../../../../foundation-models/2611.34830-jepa-eu/README-en.md) · [One-Step Prediction Fidelity Is a Poor Proxy for Planning Performance in JEPA World Models](../../../../foundation-models/2610.19375-jepa-prediction-planning/README-en.md)

### Do Agentic LongLive and PixVid modify the same layer? {#cross-cross-nov26-agentic-longlive}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. The former freezes a generator and injects memory KV at boundaries; PixVid transfers latent DiT knowledge to pixels with a detailer. External consistency memory is not VAE removal.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: a frozen latent generator can accept entity memory, while a pixel DiT still needs a separate long-horizon memory design.

    Sources: [Agentic LongLive: Asynchronous Agentic Memory for Long Video Generation](../../../../multimodal-models/2611.34907-agentic-longlive/README-en.md) · [Back to Pixels: Lifting Latent Video Diffusion into Pixel Space](../../../../multimodal-models/2611.17336-pixvid/README-en.md)
